cards.note: Baseline already ships an npm-shaped bundle (package.json dsh.bundle.patch + cordis.patch.yml insert row) installed through the profile bundle list; no repository-plugins rows, dsh.plugin.json or __ModuleLoader__ artifact exist in the tree.
No dshClient field, no dsh.plugin.json and no client half; the only dsh manifest key is dsh.bundle.patch.
Host-plane-only bundle: the plugin builds no client bundle and declares no dsh.client, so the client-modules scan never enumerates it.
The only service the plugin reads by property access (ctx.llm) is declared in inject; a cold boot on dsh-v0.1.2-alpha.2 activates the row with no pending (waiting for service: ...) line.

Conditional not met: llm is the plugin's whole capability and is mounted by dsh-base in the official profile path (base cordis.patch.yml:27), so the A1-01 field note's hard inject is the documented form; there is no meaningful degrade branch for a provider-directory read.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and derives no session state; it has one apply() effect that reads the LLM registry.
No self-rendering client half; no ctx.sessions use anywhere.
No tasks/jobs tail, no tasks.peek or tasks.read usage.
Only service identifier in the plugin is llm; no httpServer/webServer, tasks/jobs or onTaskDone/onJobDone references.
No image refs, read_image output or persisted image metadata.
The plugin registers, wraps or parses no read_image output and keeps no snapshots of it.
Not a DeepSeek adapter, image interceptor or attachment/upload cache; it only reads the provider directory.

Removed host apiProxy.llm.providers() rebased onto the same host-plane read on the domain service: inject ['llm'] + ctx.llm.listProviders() (packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:462, LlmProviderInfo types.ts:182); ctx.remote is the client plane (gateway client:153) and stays pending, and the manifest follows @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm.
Target is alpha.2, where A2-01 restores the ignorable retention semantics, and this plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents either way.
No host-source patch, no import from internal session-view paths; the plugin has no host-side patch directory at all.
No launcher wrapper, SDK/ACP integration or profile-file reader; composition is left to the official loader via dsh.bundle.patch.
Not a headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parser.
No tool presentation mode, PTC preset or dispatch waterfall usage.
No permission/approval/WebFetch policy or shipped-preset use; the bundle overlay inserts one row and touches no tool policy.
No custom loopback HTTP/WS/RPC route, browser page or /api handler; cordis.patch.yml only inserts the bundle row.
Not a model-provider plugin and ships no settings-page patch to retire.
No UI or localization resources, so no custom i18n patch exists to replace.
No subagent orchestration, selection or pass-through parameters.

Informational: the official adapter reports the loaded package name/version for this row like any other plugin, but plugin code needs no change; the fixture's migrate profile keeps the inventory row disabled outside this tree.
No shell or Windows directory-picker compatibility workaround to retire.
Deployment-level session-log egress; the plugin neither enables nor transports session logs.
No browser acceptance script or web wrapper; the plugin has no web half.
Registers no userQuestions answerer and listens on no user-questions waterfall.
No agent-preset inference, preset roots or dsh-agent-presets import.
Does not import @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm/message or compute token deltas; the dsh-llm dependency is only the manifest record of the consumed service.
The plugin is a single-row overlay bundle, not a profile/bundle maintainer reusing the dsh-base composition, and states no telemetry stance.
No direct @earendil-works/pi-ai or dsh-llm-pi-ai dependency or import, so no duplicate-instance risk.
No client half and no @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime import or dsh.client.inject entry.
No client bundle or assembly row, so the boot-manifest id contract does not apply.
Reads no session timeline, conversation nodes or user message content.
No composer DOM manipulation; no browser surface at all.
Renders no MarkdownText/CodeBlocks and imports no ui-primitives.
No ctx.connection.api use; history/transcript reads are absent.
Constructs no subagent seed/persisted descriptors and asserts no subagent/descriptor shape.
No workspace/navigation or directory-picker calls.
No third-party persisted SessionEvents produced, so the restored ignorable retention semantics have no producer here.
No ctx.remote calls: the plugin reads the host-plane domain service directly (a plain synchronous method), so RemoteResult/RemoteError branches do not exist in it.

Packaging surface: the plugin imports no runtime or type package (the llm service is consumed through inject), so there is no moved-out type package to declare and no peer, override or lockfile to prune; the single declarative @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm dependency is inert at runtime and resolves at npm (0.1.2-alpha.2 published).
No startup wrapper or CI matrix workaround for the Node 24.0-24.11.1 web defect.
Does not consume pluginInventory/list or validate PluginInventorySnapshot.
No client Remote use and no host.describe call to replace with $host.home/isLoopback.
Mounts no tool/agent packages individually and lists no peers; the profile it joins starts from the shipped dsh-base, which already mounts session-projection.
No ctx.settings.register/update/get use and no settingsNamespace import or test double.
